cards.explanation: The answer is prayed, friends. Isaiah's message opens with “Because you have prayed to Me concerning Sennacherib king of Assyria…” so the LORD is answering Hezekiah's prayer. Sennacherib was Assyria's king, the one Hezekiah prayed about. I think prayer is a pretty good thing to do when somebody that big is on your mind.

The answer is despises, friends. The word against Sennacherib says the Virgin Daughter of Zion “…despises you and mocks you…” Sennacherib was Assyria's king, the man who'd been making all the threats. Now the one he'd been looking down on is the one looking down on him.

The answer is the Holy One of Israel, friends. The LORD asks, “Whom have you taunted and blasphemed?” and then answers it Himself: “Against the Holy One of Israel!” Sennacherib was Assyria's king, and he'd been loud toward somebody way bigger than Hezekiah. Picture yelling at the wrong person for a long time before you find out who it is.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD repeats Sennacherib's bragging: “I have cut down its tallest cedars, the finest of its cypresses.” Sennacherib was Assyria's king, and he's counting trees like trophies. He talks like a man who's never once been told no.

The answer is that He planned it long ago, friends. The LORD says, “Long ago I ordained it; in days of old I planned it.” Sennacherib, Assyria's king, had been taking all the credit. The LORD says it was planned long before Sennacherib ever opened his mouth.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD says the people are “…like plants in the field, tender green shoots, grass on the rooftops, scorched before it is grown.” That's a picture of weakness, nothing like a mighty tree. Grass on a rooftop, scorched before it is grown. Not much of a tree.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD says to Sennacherib, Assyria's king, “But I know your sitting down, your going out and coming in, and your raging against Me.” The raging is right there on the LORD's list.

The answer is send him back the way he came, friends. The LORD says, “I will send you back the way you came.” Sennacherib, Assyria's king, is the one getting the hook in his nose and the bit in his mouth. I think that's a man being steered.

The answer is that they will sow and reap again, friends. The sign says, “But in the third year you will sow and reap; you will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.” Two years of eating what grows on its own, then back to planting and harvesting. Hezekiah, Judah's king, gets a clear schedule for a recovery.

The answer is True, friends. The message says, “…the surviving remnant of the house of Judah will again take root below and bear fruit above.” That's roots going down and fruit coming up. It's a picture of survivors growing again.

The answer is the zeal of the LORD of Hosts, friends. The message says, “The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this.” The remnant coming out of Jerusalem and Mount Zion is the LORD's doing. Hezekiah, Judah's king, can set his worries down on that one.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD says Sennacherib, Assyria's king, “…will not enter this city or shoot an arrow into it. He will not come before it with a shield or build up a siege ramp against it.” No arrow, no shield, no ramp. That's a pretty clear no.

The answer is for His own sake and David's, friends. The LORD says, “I will defend this city and save it for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David.” He's the One doing the defending, and He names Himself first. I think that's a good promise to hear.

The answer is Nineveh, friends. The text says Sennacherib, Assyria's king, “…returned to Nineveh and stayed there.” He broke camp and withdrew, just like the LORD said he'd go back the way he came. Nineveh is where he stayed.

The answer is Ararat, friends. The text says Adrammelech and Sharezer, Sennacherib's sons, “…escaped to the land of Ararat.” This is a heavy part of the passage, so I'll just say it plainly. Ararat is the land the text names.
The answer is Esar-haddon, friends. The text says, “And his son Esar-haddon reigned in his place.” Sennacherib's son takes the throne. That's all this passage tells us about him.
